title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source: Embraer A-29 Super Tucano aircraft On-Call Support
description: 1. DESCRIPTION: The Department of the Air Force, Air Force Test Center (AFTC), Specialized Test Contracting (PZZD) at Edwards Air Force Base, CA, intends to award a sole-source Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract for Embraer A-29 Super Tucano aircraft On-Call Support. Three (3) fully sealed Embraer A-29 Super Tucano aircraft are currently in storage at Edwards Air Force Base (AFB), California. These aircraft are not expected to return to flight for use by the Air Force. However, on-call maintenance support is required to address limited conditions affecting safe storage, environmental compliance, and ground movement within the installation. The contractor shall furnish all management, labor, supervision, tools, equipment, repair parts, consumables, transportation, and travel required to perform on-call services, except for items expressly identified as Government-furnished. Services under this PWS are limited to non-recurring, as-needed actions associated with, Fuel, hydraulic, and/or oil leak repair or mitigation, Tire repair or replacement, Ground towing and repositioning of aircraft; and Related minor maintenance actions necessary to place the aircraft in a safe storage or towable condition. This effort is intended solely to support stored aircraft in a non-flight status. 2. SOLE SOURCE AUTHORITY: The proposed acquisition will be conducted under the simplified acquisition procedures of Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 13.1, as authorized by RFO 13.106-1(b)(1), Soliciting from a Single Source. The Government intends to award this requirement as a sole-source contract to: Proposed Contractor: Sierra Nevada Company LLC CAGE Code: 6ZVZ8 UEI: G1YKV4VHL8Q5 Socioeconomic Status: Large Business Address: 1150 N Eglin PKWY, Shalimar, Florida 32579-1227 3. TECHNICAL JUSTIFICATION & MARKET RESEARCH FINDINGS: Comprehensive market research conducted under RFO Part 10 has determined that Sierra Nevada Company LLC is the only commercial source capable of satisfying this requirement without the Government incurring unacceptable technical and schedule risks. Unique Technical Expertise: Sierra Nevada Company LLC is a U.S.-based aerospace and defense technology provider delivering mission?ready solutions across multiple domains, with a strong focus on integration, ISR, and multi?domain command and control. The specialize in Aircraft Integration & Modification; Modular, mission?tailored aircraft system design and modification, e.g., M?28 Special Operations Multi?Role Aircraft (SOMA), RAPCON?X� aerial ISR platform. The company's work supports aerospace, national security, and mission?critical integration needs, emphasizing agility, rapid innovation, and interoperability across domains. RFI Results: A Sources Sought FA930427Q5001 was posted to SAM.gov seeking feedback on the draft PWS. Received 0 responses. Interagency Non-Viability: Market research has not found any additional suitable parties, requiring the Air Force to execute a BOA directly to the sole source. 4. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES: This publication is for informational purposes only and does not constitute a formal Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quote (RFQ). No solicitation package is available. However, in accordance with RFO Part 5, any interested party that believes it possesses the technical capability to meet this requirement may submit a written capability statement. Capability statements must provide clear, documented evidence of the vendor's prior experience with the requirement. All submissions received within five (5) calendar days of the publication of this notice will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether a competitive procurement is in the best interest of the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Contracting Officer. Points of Contact Primary Contracting Officer: Thomas J. Shea Email: thomas.shea.3@us.af.mil Alternate Contracting Officer: Marc A. Venzon Email: marc_anthony.venzon@us.af.mil

title: Dry Ice Cleaning and Inspection of Forward Ventilation System onboard Virginia Class Submarine
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with simplified acquisition procedures found in the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Revolutionary Far Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 12.2, effective 1 February 2026, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation whereby quotations are being requested. This solicitation is intended to result in the issuance of a singular firm fixed price award. Solicitation Number N62789-27-Q-0003 is issued as an urgent request for quotation (RFQ). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular FAC-2026-01 with an effective date of 13 March 2026. NAICS Code: 336611, size standard: 1,300 Each vendor must submit proof of their NAVSEA approved ventilation cleaning procedure in order to be considered for this award. Failure to have a NAVSEA approved cleaning process will result in immediate disqualification. See statement of work paragraph 3.1. Each person accessing the workspace, onboard a Virginia Class Submarine, must currently hold a valid secret security clearance. Failure to hold a valid secret security clearance will result in immediate disqualification. See statement of work paragraph 3.8. Each vendor must also be CMMC Level 1; Self Certified within the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Supplier Performance Risk System Module. Additional details and registration instructions are contained in the Solicitation. CLIN 0001: Labor. Vendor shall complete inspection and cleaning of the ventilation system tied to the ships galley and the number two electrostatic participator (ESP) in accordance with the enclosed statement of work. Vendor to state number of people, their relative job title(s) and estimated timeline for completing these efforts. CLIN 0002: Equipment/Material. Equipment/Material including consumable related costs (PPE, cleaning agents, disposal costs etc.) associated with this statement of work. Vendor shall clearly list and describe any and all equipment costs and/or material/consumable expenses to be incurred. CLIN 0003: Travel. Travel related costs associated with the vendor completing this statement of work. Vendor shall clearly list and describe the number of people traveling along with their relative travel expenses to be incurred (lodging, meals/incidentals, mileage/flight expenses etc). TAKE NOTE OF REQUIREMENT FOR ENTRY TO THE FACILITY PER PARAGRAPH 4.0 �ACCESS REQUIREMENTS� IN SECTON C OF THE SOLICITATION Quotes are due prior to 5:00PM EST, 13 November 2027. Late submissions will not be accepted. The Government will evaluate the total offers for award purposes by adding the total price for all line items. Evaluation of all line items will not obligate the Government to award all line items. The Government intends to evaluate proposals and award a contract without discussions with offerors. However, the Government reserves the right to conduct discussions if later determined by the Contracting Officer to be necessary. The Government reserves the right to award one line, all line items or any combination thereof. If multiple line items are awarded, costs/prices for each line item will be totaled and award amount will be based on that total. Award will be given to the responsible offeror whose offer, conforming to the solicitation, is determined to be the lowest priced technically acceptable offer. Offerors must satisfy the requirements described in the performance criteria, as well as other RFQ requirements. Offers that take exception to any performance criteria are unacceptable. To be considered technically acceptable, offers must adhere to the requirements described within the statement of work. See attached statement of work for more details. Offers should be submitted via electronic commerce. The electronic address for receipt of offers is: andrea.a.cook.civ@us.navy.mil and stephanie.l.neale.civ@us.navy.mil. Offerors should identify the RFQ number in the Subject Line of the email. Offerors are advised to submit electronic documents early and confirm successful transmission/receipt. The System for Award Management (SAM) is a government-maintained database of companies wanting to do business with the Government. A firm must register and be active in SAM to receive a Federal Award. Register at: https://sam.gov/SAM/pages/public/index.jsf.

IBM ESS Renewal for Idaho National Laboratory
description: I. INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL). BEA is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from prospective offerors to support IBM ESS renewal for INL�s IBM High-Performance Computer. II. BACKGROUND INL is a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratory dedicated to nuclear energy, national security, and clean energy innovation. INL conducts research and operational activities requiring secure, compliant, and reliable software solutions. BEA is identifying qualified small businesses that can supply IBM Storage Scale Systems warranty renewal services. III. SCOPE OF WORK Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), as the Management and Operating Contractor for Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking qualified small business vendors authorized by IBM to provide renewal services for the IBM Elastic Storage System (ESS) and IBM Storage Scale System supporting INL's High-Performance Computing (HPC) environment. The selected contractor shall provide warranty, maintenance, software support, and media retention services for the IBM ESS infrastructure identified in this EOI. Services shall include all applicable hardware and software support coverage required to maintain operational availability, vendor support eligibility, and lifecycle management of the existing IBM storage environment. Required Services The contractor shall: Provide IBM-authorized renewal of maintenance and support coverage for the identified IBM ESS hardware and software assets. Maintain all manufacturer-provided warranty, repair, technical support, and software maintenance entitlements throughout the period of performance. Provide required hardware support service levels, including Advanced Support and On-Site Repair (Next Business Day, 9x5) coverage, as specified in Section IV. Provide software support services, including Media Retention and Normal Business Hours support coverage, as identified in Section IV. Ensure all support agreements remain active and continuous for the required coverage period and all option years. Coordinate directly with IBM, as required, for service entitlement verification, contract administration, warranty renewals, software maintenance, and technical support. Provide annual pricing for the base year and each option year. Include media retention services for all covered systems throughout the base period and all option years. Provide documentation identifying all applicable support entitlements, contract numbers, service levels, and coverage periods associated with the renewed services. IV. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested small businesses should submit an Expression of Interest that includes the following: Company name and point of contact Description of software products and solutions currently offered Relevant experience providing software products, licensing, or technical support services Authorization to procure services through IBM including, IBM Elastic Storage System (ESS) and IBM Storage Scale System NAICS codes and business size classification Active SAM.gov registration status Small Businesses shall provide a quote with 3-option years. Required Coverage and Option Years Required Coverage: 10/01/2026-10/01/2027 Option Year 2: 10/01/2027-10/01/2028 Option Year 3: 10/01/2028-10/01/2029 Quotes must be valid for at least 30 days. IBM ESS Renewal shall include media retention for all 3 and yearly payments. Required IBM ESS Renewal services are as follows: SEE PDF FOR TABLE LISTING OF HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE Deadline for submission: by end of day November 13, 2026 Submit to: Chase.Egbert@inl.gov V. PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified small businesses able to meet INL software acquisition needs. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. Because information received in response to this EOI may be business sensitive or proprietary to the responding party, respondents must mark information in their responses accordingly.

description: Sources Sought Laundry and Dry-Cleaning Services THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. The 379th Contracting Squadron is conducting market research to determine interest and capability of potential sources. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. The 379th Contracting Squadron is seeking potential sources for the purchase of Laundry and Dry-Cleaning services in the Qatar and Saudi Arabia regions. Please see Attachments 1, 2 and 3 for complete list of areas to be covered. The recommended North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) Code is 812320 - Cleaners, drycleaning and laundry service (except coin-operated) with a size standard of $8M. � If there is a NAICS code that you believe would be more applicable, please provide with your capability statement. If so, what are they? 2. If it is required to conduct a site visit prior to contract award, approximately how many business days would it take your company to prepare the site for a visit by government representatives? 3. Do you have experience handling and cleaning contaminated medical linen? If so, to whom and for how long? Describe your experience adhering to regulations for handling and cleaning medical linen. 4. Do you have dedicated equipment and processes for handling contaminated medical linen separately from other laundry? Describe the segregation process. 5. Describe your quality control procedures to ensure that linen is thoroughly cleaned, disinfected, and free of damage. 6. Describe your transportation methods for both soiled and clean linen and how often do you sanitize your transport vehicles? 7. Are you able to handle specialized cleaning needs, such as stain removal or repairs? 8. Do you have a system for monitoring and controlling water temperature and chemical concentrations during the washing process? 9. Do you intend to provide a quote for this requirement? How many days would you need to draft a quote? Provide any additional questions or comments related to the requirement. All responses will be posted. This Sources Sought Announcement is solely for informational and planning purposes only and is not a solicitation or Request for Quote. Please send responses to: SrA Dominique Henry, Contracting Officer, Dominique.henry.1@us.af.mil no later than 12:00PM Arabian Standard Time on 14 November, 2025.

In accordance with FAR subpart 13.5 and 41 U.S.C. 1901, the Bureau of Engraving and Printing (BEP) Office of the Treasury Common Services Center (TCSC) on behalf of its Office of Quality Operations intends to award a sole source contract to Authentix, Inc. for Quality Evaluation Detectors (QED) Preventative and Remedial Maintenance Service. Authentix Inc. is the sole-source provider of all services related to the Quality Evaluation Detector (QED). Because the systems are proprietary and require access to classified information for proper servicing, Authentix does not engage third-party vendors to perform system-level services. The anticipated Period of Performance is for one (1) twelve-month base period and four (4) twelve-month option periods. The places of performance will be performed at the contractor's repair depot location. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive offers/quotes/proposals. A determination not to compete this requirement is solely within the discretion of the government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The solicitation will not be posted. To be considered, responses must be received NO LATER THAN 4:00PM EST, November 14, 2026. Additionally, interested sources must be registered and currently active in the System for Award Management (SAM), found at https://www.sam.gov. Responses MUST be submitted within the closing date/time of publication of this notice. Point of Contact regarding this notice is Contracting Officer Laqulla Williams, at Laqulla.Williams@bep.gov.

title: MH-60S Service Life Extension Program (SLEP) Kits
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) intends to negotiate and award a Sole Source Delivery order under and pursuant to the terms and conditions of Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) N0001923G0002 to Lockheed Martin Rotary and Mission Systems (LM RMS) in Owego, NY for the procurement of airframe structural modification, replacement, and avionics wiring harness kits in support of the MH-60S Service Life Extension Program (SLEP). The SLEP addresses specific USN MH-60S aircraft system/components that are not forecasted to meet current service life requirements. The projected period of performance for this requirement forty-eight (48) months from contract award. This action is intended to be awarded on a sole source basis to Lockheed Martin Rotary and Mission Systems (LM RMS) under the authority permitting other than full and open competition, Title 10, U.S.C. 3204 (a)(1), as implemented by Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1, "Only One Responsible Source and No Other type of Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements." LM RMS is the sole designer, developer, systems integrator, and manufacturer of the MH-60S aircraft and weapon system and, as such, is the only source with the requisite knowledge and skilled personnel, facilities, manufacturing tooling, test equipment, experience, and technical data necessary to provide the required supplies and services. Note: This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. The proposed contract action is for supplies or services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under authority of Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.103-1. The Government does not intend to fund the development or qualification of other sources for fulfilling this requirement, as production for the supplies listed requires a substantial initial investment or an extended period of preparation for manufacture. However, the Government will consider all proposals received within fifteen (15) days after the publication of this synopsis. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Questions concerning subcontracting opportunities should be directed to Jim Boulay at jim.s.boulay@lmco.com Lockheed Martin Rotary and Mission Systems, 1801 State Route 17 C, Owego, NY 13827.

title: MUX/MALE Engineering Logistics Support (ELS) Follow-On
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), Patuxent River, MD, intends to negotiate and award an Order under a Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) with General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc (GA-ASI) to provide comprehensive Engineering Logistics Support (ELS) for the Marine Air-Ground Task Force (MAGTF) Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Expeditionary / Medium Altitude / Long Endurance (MUX/MALE) program, aiming to ensure the operational readiness, sustainment, and continuous improvement of USMC-unique payloads and systems. This critical support encompasses a broad range of activities including, but not limited to, program management, logistics, spares analysis, engineering services (e.g., troubleshooting, non-standard maintenance, configuration management, Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs), reach-back), lead systems integration (LSI), Field Maintenance Artisans (FMAs), Logistics Support Representatives (LSRs), Payload Operator Training, Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages (DMSMS) mitigation, airworthiness, cybersecurity, software sustainment, and technical data management. The proposed contract action is a follow-on effort for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) and FAR Overhaul 6.103-1, "Only One Responsible Source and No Other Type of Supplies or Services will Satisfy Agency Requirements." GA-ASI is the sole designer, developer, manufacturer, and integrator of the MQ-9, and therefore, is the only contractor with the requisite knowledge, experience, and technical data that can meet the Government's requirements on a timely basis and in a cost-effective manner. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. Interested parties, however, may identify their interest and capability by responding to the requirement. The Government will consider all information received prior to the closing date of this synopsis. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed contract action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. No phone inquiries will be entertained. Responses shall be made in writing by E-mail to the attention of Ms. Sarah Fyock or Ms. Sharina Miller using the contact information provided in this synopsis. Companies interested in subcontracting opportunities should contact GA-ASI directly at GA-ASISmall-Business@ga-asi.com.

title: Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) 2026 Announcement
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) seeks innovative approaches to address challenges related to quantum computing. The Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) aims to examine approaches for constructing a utility-scale fault-tolerant quantum computer and computational workflows that include quantum compute steps. Proposed research should investigate approaches that enable revolutionary advances in design, engineering, test, and evaluation of such systems. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice. To rapidly capitalize on new opportunities, DARPA announces the QBI 2026 opportunity, which seeks specific solutions to targeted challenges related to developing utility-scale quantum computers, as defined in specific QBI topic (QBIT) calls. Each QBIT will (1) outline specific details regarding the research topic of interest and (2) provide proposal and submission instructions, including the due date for proposal submission, in addition to those outlined in this PA. Proposals must only be submitted in response to a QBIT. Proposals submitted directly to this PA will not be considered.

Tuleva hankinta koskee kaikkia Jyväskylän kaupungin toimialoja ja liikelaitoksia. Tarjouskilpailulla muodostetaan 15 yrityksen/toimijan pooli, tai useamman, mikäli mukaan ei saada vähintään 25 valmentajaa. Jos soveltuvia tarjouksia on vähemmän kuin 15, valitaan kaikki soveltuvat tarjoukset. Jotta turvataan pientenkin toimijoiden pääseminen hankintaan mukaan, rinnakkaisia tarjouksia ei hyväksytä, ja yksi yritys/toimija voi tarjota 1-3 asiantuntijaa pooliin. Palvelun käynnistämisen tavoiteaika on 1.3.2027. Lisätiedot hankinnan kohteesta tarjouspyynnöstä ja sen liitteistä.

description: Hankinnan kohteena on Jyväskylän kaupungin henkilöstöön kuuluvien esimiesten ja työyhteisöjen osaamisen kehittämisen palvelut. Hankintaa ei ole jaettu osiin, sillä jakaminen ei palvelun luonteen vuoksi ole tarkoituksenmukaista eikä jaosta saada selkeää. Sen sijaan poolista tehdään melko suuri, jotta saadaan laaja-alainen asiantuntijuus turvattua. Palveluiden hankinta voidaan toteuttaa joko henkilöstöhallinnon tai työyksiköiden esimiesten hankkimana tilanteissa, joissa on havaittu kehittämistarvetta. Tuleva hankinta koskee kaikkia Jyväskylän kaupungin toimialoja ja liikelaitoksia. Tarjouskilpailulla muodostetaan 15 yrityksen/toimijan pooli, tai useamman, mikäli mukaan ei saada vähintään 25 valmentajaa. Jos soveltuvia tarjouksia on vähemmän kuin 15, valitaan kaikki soveltuvat tarjoukset. Jotta turvataan pientenkin toimijoiden pääseminen hankintaan mukaan, rinnakkaisia tarjouksia ei hyväksytä, ja yksi yritys/toimija voi tarjota 1-3 asiantuntijaa pooliin. Palvelun käynnistämisen tavoiteaika on 1.3.2027. Lisätiedot hankinnan kohteesta tarjouspyynnöstä ja sen liitteistä.

description: VHAPG Part 806.3 OFOC Page 1 of 4 Revision: 04 Effective Date: 12/15/25 Acquisition ID#: 36C24C-26-AP-0554 siDEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS Justification and Approval (J&A) For Other Than Full and Open Competition Acquisition Plan Action ID: 36C24C-26-AP-0554 Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA); Regional Procurement Office Central (RPOC); 1639 Medical Center Parkway, Suite 204; Murfreesboro, TN 37129. Funding ID: F36C134-26-0000073 Nature and/or Description of the Action Being Approved: Firm-fixed price contract for expert witness and consulting services for defending a contract dispute pending Civilian Board of Contract Appeals (CBCA) where expert services for a medical recovery audit contract is needed. Description of Supplies/Services Required to Meet the Agency s Needs: VA OGC has a new requirement for expert witness litigation support services from XXXX XXXXXX, of LitCon Group, LLC in support of ongoing litigation of CBCA Claims 7718, 8054 and 8056, Alexander CPA, PLLC v Department of Veterans Affairs. The expert witness shall perform the following services: Review and analyze the Appellant's expert report(s) and the supporting data, methodologies, and assumptions relied upon, including any damages model and any opinions concerning industry-standard practices; Review relevant contract documentation, including the contract and its Performance Work Statement, the contingency-fee payment structure, the task order/ordering mechanism, the Feasibility Assessment Report requirements, claim denial and compliant-payment data, and applicable correspondence and administrative record materials provided by VA counsel; Evaluate the reliability and validity of the opposing expert's damages calculations, including the reasonableness of recovery projections derived from collected/closed claim populations, treatment of the contingency-fee model, assumptions regarding recoverable amounts, causation linking alleged VA conduct to claimed losses, and any failure to account for contract terms limiting or conditioning recovery (e.g., task-order issuance contingent on feasibility results, exclusions of certain claim categories, refund-request offsets, and cessation of payment six months after task order expiration); Prepare a written rebuttal report stating the expert's opinions, the bases and reasons for them, the facts and data considered, and the expert's qualifications, consistent with the standards applicable to expert reports before the CBCA; Provide deposition and hearing testimony as required and prepare for such testimony; Assist with VA s preparation for the deposition of Appellant s expert and assistance with VA s trial preparation; Assist with VA s preparation for, and attendance at, ADR, should one be conducted; and Consult with VA counsel throughout the engagement and respond to follow-up analytical requests as needed. Estimated value is $XXXXXXXXX. Due to the nature of trial litigation, it will not be possible at the time of awarding the contract to accurately estimate the extent or duration of the work or anticipate costs with any reasonable degree of confidence. However, based on the prior level of effort required under similar contracts, the nature of the pending litigation, and current hourly rates, the VA thinks a six-month period of performance will meet the Government s requirement. Statutory Authority Permitting Other than Full and Open Competition: Industrial Mobilization, Engineering, Developmental or Research Capability or Expert Services per 41 USC §3304(a)(3) as implemented by RFO 6.103-3. Demonstration that the Contractor s Unique Qualifications or Nature of the Acquisition Requires the Use of the Authority Cited Above (applicability of authority): 10 U.S.C 3204(a)(3)(C), as prescribed in RFO 6.302-3, Industrial Mobilization, Engineering, Developmental or Research Capability or Expert Services states, to procure the services of an expert for use, in litigation or dispute (including any reasonably foreseeable litigation or dispute) involving the Federal Government, in any trial, hearing, or proceeding before any court, administrative tribunal, or agency, or to procure the services of an expert or neutral for use in any part of an alternate dispute resolution or negotiated rulemaking process, whether or not the expert is expected to testify. The specific statutory and RFO citations authorize the Government to award a contract using non-competitive means to use experts in any litigation involving the Government. XXXX XXXXXX of LitCon Group, LLC has been determined by OGC to have the unique expertise in the issues underlying the litigation that meets the government s needs. More specifically, Mr. Lesch has demonstrated experience quantifying damages in commercial or government contract disputes, preferably involving contingency-fee or recovery-based compensation models, relevant professional credentials, which shall include one of the following: CPA, FHFMA, FACHE, CFE, ASA/CVA or comparable valuation or forensic accounting certifications, and prior experience serving as a testifying expert, with the ability to withstand examination and to produce reports admissible before the CBCA, federal courts, or boards of contract appeals. Description of Efforts Made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as possible (including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by RFO Part 5 and, if not, which exception under RFO Part 5 applies): XXXX XXXXX of LitCon Group LLCs unique expertise in the issues underlying the litigation and the specific statutory and regulatory authority to award sole source contracts to experts and consultants when the Government is involved in litigation obviates the need for efforts to obtain competition. The Government is entitled to the experts and consultants that will best help the Government in ongoing litigation. Determination by the CO that the Anticipated Cost to the Government will be Fair and Reasonable: Pricing will be determined fair and reasonable based on price analysis techniques identified in RFO Part 15-404-1(5), Comparison of proposed prices with the independent Government cost estimate. Description of the Market Research Conducted and the Results, or a Statement of the Reasons Market Research Was Not Conducted: On August 3, 2026, the SBA Small Business Database was queried, utilizing NAICS 561492 to identify SBA certified SDVOSB and VOSB concerns. 146 SDVOSB and VOSB concerns were identified. On August 18, 2026, Special Notice Intent to Sole Source 36C24C26Q0028 was posted to SAM.gov, with a response due date of August 24, 2026, by 12:00pm (Eastern). The notice states that while not a request for competitive quotes, any responsible source who believes it is capable of meeting the requirements may submit a capability statement. All SDVOSB and VOSB concerns identified in the SBA Small Business query were emailed the link to the Special Notice. Four (4) responses were received. Mandatory sources were consulted; however, none meet the Government s requirements as they do not offer these services. XXXXX XXXXXX of LitCon Group LLC has unique experience and knowledge of this type of litigation. title: JP Murtha Float Mooring Bitts Retrofit
description: JP Murtha Float Mooring Bitts Retrofit - The United States Army Corps of Engineers, (USACE) Pittsburgh District has a requirement for the retrofitting of existing hydraulic structures within an active navigation lock. The Prime Contractor must be capable of executing complex in-the-wet construction, specifically: The John P. Murtha Floating Mooring Bitt Retrofit consists of the installation of Government furnished Floating Mooring Bitts into Contractor fabricated embedded frame on the existing River Chamber Middle Wall. In-the-wet construction methods are required. Design, fabrication, and installation of two dewatering boxes are required for installation of the Floating Mooring Bitts. Removal or alterations to existing work in such a manner as to prevent injury or damage to any portions of the existing work which remain. Repair or replace portions of existing work which have been altered during construction operations to match existing or adjoining work, as approved by the Contracting Officer. At the completion of operations, existing work must be in a condition equal to or better than that which existed before new work started. To achieve this Requirement the Contractor must: a. Floating Plant Operations: Providing, operating, and mooring a fully compliant floating plant (crane/deck barge and push boat) in an active river chamber in accordance with EM 385-1-1. b. Dewatering Box (Cofferdam): Fabricating, installing, and sealing structural steel dewatering boxes against lock monoliths for a strict maximum duration of 90 days. c. Heavy Demolition and Concrete Work: Executing concrete wire-sawing, core drilling, and demolition of existing lock wall recesses, followed by cast-in-place concrete integration. d. Structural Steel and Mooring Bitts: Fabricating heavy steel embedded anchorage frames, and salvaging/installing Government-Furnished Floating Mooring Bitts. e. Commercial Diving: Providing certified commercial dive teams to support underwater inspection, rigging, and cofferdam sealing. The work shall be completed within 730 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed. This acquisition will be procured as an Unrestricted Full and Open Solicitation. The resulting award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Construction Contract. All responsible Bidders are encouraged to participate. title: High-Capacity Hydrogen and Hydrogen Isotope Getters
description: Even small amounts of hydrogen can damage sensitive equipment over time. As hydrogen accumulates inside sealed environments, it can corrode metals, weaken structural materials, degrade electronic components, and, in some applications, create explosion hazards. Preventing that buildup is essential for maintaining the reliability and safety of many high-value systems. Hydrogen getters are materials built into sealed devices and systems to remove hydrogen before it can accumulate. Like a moisture absorber, they remove an unwanted gas. Instead of trapping water, however, they chemically react with hydrogen and lock it away permanently. Depending on the application, a getter may take the form of a pellet, coating, thin film, powder, or printable material. Many commercially available getters rely on zirconium-based materials that offer limited hydrogen storage capacity, require activation before use, or operate effectively only within a narrow temperature range. Some also depend on costly vacuum-deposition manufacturing processes that limit design flexibility. Los Alamos researchers have developed a new class of hydrogen getters designed to overcome these limitations. The materials capture hydrogen and its isotopes, including deuterium and tritium, across a broad range of operating conditions without requiring activation while offering significantly higher storage capacity and greater flexibility for manufacturing and product integration. Value Proposition Hydrogen can quietly build up inside sealed devices and industrial systems, shortening equipment life and creating safety risks. Los Alamos National Laboratory has developed a new class of high-capacity hydrogen getters that permanently remove hydrogen before it causes damage. Compared with conventional getters, this technology stores more hydrogen, operates across a wider range of conditions, and can be manufactured in multiple forms for easy integration into commercial products. Hydrogen uptake rate decreases as getter materials fill with hydrogen. Compared with a conventional getter (brown), the LANL high-capacity getter (green) maintains rapid hydrogen capture over a much larger storage capacity. Advantages Stores significantly more hydrogen than many conventional getter materials. Permanently removes hydrogen, improving long-term reliability in sealed systems. Operates across a broad temperature range without activation. Captures hydrogen even at pressures well below atmospheric levels. Selectively removes hydrogen in mixed-gas environments. Hydrogen uptake rates can be tailored to specific applications. Compatible with polymers and available as films, coatings, pellets, powders, strands, and printable pastes for flexible product integration. Reduces projected material and manufacturing costs compared with many zirconium-based getter technologies. Scalable manufacturing supports applications ranging from miniature electronics to large industrial systems. Technology Description The getter materials chemically react with hydrogen and its isotopes to form stable compounds that permanently lock the hydrogen inside the material, providing long-term protection for sealed devices and industrial equipment. The technology is based on a novel organic alkyne chemistry. Alkynes are carbon-containing molecules that readily react with hydrogen, allowing the material to store substantially more hydrogen than many conventional getter systems. Unlike many commercial getters, these materials operate without activation and continue to perform across a broad temperature range. They also selectively capture hydrogen in the presence of gases such as helium, nitrogen, argon, and methane, making them well suited for complex industrial and vacuum environments. The hydrogen capture rate can be tailored by adjusting the catalyst formulation for specific operating conditions. Hydrogen capture has also been demonstrated at pressures well below atmospheric conditions, expanding the range of potential applications. The materials are compatible with polymers and other common manufacturing materials, allowing them to be incorporated into films, coatings, pellets, powders, strands, adhesives, foams, and printable pastes. description: L'enquête suisse sur la population active (ESPA) est une enquête auprès des personnes qui est réalisée chaque année depuis 1991. Le but principal de l'ESPA est de fournir des données sur la structure de la population active et sur les comportements en matière d'activité professionnelle. Grâce à l'application stricte de définitions internationales, les données de la Suisse peuvent être comparées avec celles des pays de l'OCDE et de l'Union européenne. Depuis 2010, l'ESPA se déroule en continu. Enquête suisse sur la population active (ESPA) | Office fédéral de la statistique - OFS <https://www.bfs.admin.ch/bfs/fr/home/statistiques/travail-remuneration/enquetes/espa.html> L'appel d'offres porte sur les prestations suivantes : - Mise en œuvre l'ESPA en multimode (CAWI et CATI) selon les spécifications du « responsive web design », sur la base d'un questionnaire fourni par l’OFS. Cela comprend la mise en œuvre des thèmes supplémentaires, la préparation (notamment la programmation), la réalisation (y compris la gestion des adresses et une hotline téléphonique), le monitoring, l'évaluation et le traitement des résultats des entretiens pour les années suivantes : > 2027 : Préparation et réalisation des enquêtes pilotes ESPA en mixed mode, y compris la gestion des adresses, la hotline téléphonique et l'analyse des enquêtes pilotes. > 2028 : Réalisation de l'ESPA pour une partie de l'échantillon, sans modules thématiques > 2029 : Répétition de l'ESPA, y compris 2 modules thématiques > 2030 : Répétition de l'ESPA, y compris 2 modules thématiques > 2031 : Répétition de l'ESPA, y compris 1 à 2 modules thématiques > 2032 : Répétition de l'ESPA, y compris 2 modules thématiques > 2033 : Répétition de l'ESPA pour une partie de l'échantillon (complétude des vagues), y compris 1 à 2 modules thématiques > 2034 : Répétition de l'ESPA pour une partie de l'échantillon (complétude des vagues), sans modules thématiques - Préparation, réalisation et évaluation de prétests CATI pour les années 2028 à 2032

description: Gävle kommun har idag två separata avtal avseende arbetskläder (yrkes-, varsel-, skydds- och flamskyddande kläder) samt arbetsskor, där totalt fyra (4) Leverantörer är antagna, två (2) Leverantörer per avtal. Avtalen är fördelade enligt följande: Avtal 1: Arbetskläder för kost, lokalvård och omvårdnad Avtal 2: Yrkes-, varsel-, skydds- och flamskyddande arbetskläder Inför kommande upphandling har Gävle kommun valt att tillgodose huvuddelen av behovet av arbetskläder inom vård- och omsorgsverksamheten genom ett separat avtal för hyrda arbetskläder inklusive cirkulationstvätt. En ensam Leverantör bedöms ge verksamheterna en enklare beställningsprocess, minska den administrativa hanteringen samt skapa bättre förutsättningar för en effektiv avtalsförvaltning, uppföljning och utveckling av avtalet under avtalsperioden.

title: 7th Fleet Welder Qualification and Sustained Capability Program
description: This is a Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought notice. This announcement is published for market research and planning purposes only and does not constitute a formal Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotation (RFQ). The Department of the Navy is issuing this RFI to identify sources interested in and qualified to fulfill a capability gap for welding to support ship repair and maintenance located within the 7th Fleet Area of Responsibility (AOR), excluding Hawaii. The Government intends to evaluate capabilities and draft plans to determine the feasibility of awarding Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contracts under FAR Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services). This RFI provides industry with the opportunity to review the draft requirements, propose tentative technical approaches, and provide high-level pricing and performance timelines. Clarification questions (Form J-1) shall be submitted in writing via email no later than 2 Nov 2026, 10:00AM Singapore time. RFI submission deadline is 15 Nov 2026, 10:00 AM Singapore time. Please include the team's email in your responses: flcyc257@us.navy.mil

title: Digitalt stoffkartotek
description: BESKRIVELSE AV LEVERANSEN (se vedlagte dokumenter for full beskrivelse) IKT Agder, som oppdragsgiver for denne konkurransen, gjennomfører en anskaffelse av en felles, skybasert løsning (SaaS) for digitalt stoffkartotek. Løsningen skal benyttes av Agder fylkeskommune, deltakende kommuner og øvrige virksomheter omfattet av anskaffelsen. Anskaffelsen skal bidra til bedre etterlevelse av lov- og forskriftskrav knyttet til håndtering av kjemi-kalier, styrke virksomhetenes arbeid med HMS og internkontroll, samt legge til rette for en mer stan-dardisert, effektiv og kostnadseffektiv forvaltning på tvers av de deltakende virksomhetene. Løsningen skal blant annet understøtte registrering og håndtering av kjemikalier, tilgang til og oppda-tering av sikkerhetsdatablader (SDS), risikovurderinger, eksponeringsregister, rapportering og rolle- og tilgangsstyring. Agder fylkeskommune kunngjør bare konkurransen på vegne av IKT-Agder som er oppdragsgiver.

title: Norway – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Digital substance register
description: DESCRIPTION OF THE DELIVERY (see the attached documents for a full description). ICT Agder, as the contracting authority for this competition, is carrying out a procurement of a joint, cloud based system (SaaS) for the digital substance register. The system shall be used by Agder county, participating municipalities and other entities included in the procurement. The procurement shall contribute to better compliance with legal and regulation requirements connected to handling chemistry calies, strengthen the entities ́ work with HSE and internal control, as well as facilitate a more stan-dardised, efficient and cost efficient management across the participating entities. The system shall, among other things, support registration and handling of chemicals, access to and monitoring safety data sheets (SDS), risk assessments, exposure register, reporting and role and access management. Agder county is only announcing the competition on behalf of ICT-Agder, the contracting authority.

title: Finland – Installation services (except software) – Rovaniemen Verkko Oy:n vuosien 2027–2028 sähköenergiamittarien massavaihdon yksikköhintaurakka
description: Rovaniemen Verkko Oy pyytää sitovaa yksikköhintaista urakkatarjousta Rovaniemen Verkko Oy:n vuosien 2027–2028 sähköenergiamittarien massavaihdon toteutuksesta mukana olevien liitteiden ja tarjouspyyntöasiakirjojen mukaisesti. Vuosien 2027–2028 aikana vaihdetaan Rovaniemen Verkon sähköenergiamittareita AMR 2.0 kelpoisiksi. Tilaaja hankkii vaihtotyössä tarvittavat mittarit, antennit ja sinetit. Kaiken muun materiaalin hankinta kuuluu Toimittajalle. Vaihtotyö toteutetaan Rovaniemen Verkko Oy:n verkkoalueella. Urakkaan sisältyy vaihdettavia Aidon 5000- ja 6000-sarjan suoria sähköenergiamittareita noin 9500 kpl. Yksikkömäärä on arvio eikä ole tilaajaa sitova. Urakassa noudatetaan rakennusurakan yleisiä sopimusehtoja (YSE1998) tässä urakkaohjelmassa mahdollisesti mainittuja poikkeuksia lukuun ottamatta. Urakasta solmitaan erillinen urakkasopimus. Urakoitsija vastaa tilaajan teettämien suunnitelmien ja muiden suunnitelmien yhteensovittamisesta kaikilta osin (poikkeus YSE:stä).

title: Military Recruiting Lease for office space 5,300 to 5,800 SF required
description: The Honolulu District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is soliciting lease proposals for 5,300 to 5,800 of gross rentable square feet of office and related space in Honolulu, Hawaii for Armed Forces Recruiting purposes. The U.S. Government, by and through USACE, currently occupies office and related space under a lease, in the city and state specified above. The Lessor shall provide adequate/assigned parking for approximately twelve (12) Government vehicles both during the day and overnight. The lease term is four (4) years eleven (11) months with Government termination rights and will be a full-service lease (to include all utilities and janitorial services). Delineated area: The Government requests Space in Honolulu, Hawaii in an area bounded as follows: North: River St. South: Ward Ave. East: Ala Moana Blvd. West: S. Vinyard Blvd. Buildings that have frontage on the boundary streets are deemed to be within the Delineated Area. If awarded to a new location, this office would be relocated immediately upon completion of construction to accommodate all requirements pertaining to the FY26 Construction Specifications for TAOC Offices with the lease start date commencing upon acceptance of space by the government (see attached construction specifications). Space Minimum requirements include: 1. 24-hour unrestricted access to Leased space; 2. Availability of all communications infrastructure for to include DSL, T1 or a satellite dish; 3. Direct access to secondary exterior exit door from Lease space; common area exterior exit door if shared with other military services; or exterior exit door can, and will be installed prior to occupying the facility; and 4. 24-hour lighted parking for up to twelve (12) Government vehicles and adequate parking for privately owned vehicles onsite or within a 4 block radius of the premises. Electronic Offer Submission: Offers must be submitted electronically via email to: amy.capwell@usace.army.mil Offers are due on or before: November 15, 2026. Any questions regarding this solicitation may be directed to the Primary Point of Contact listed in the �Contact Information� section of this notice. To be responsive, your offer should be based on all the terms, conditions, and responsibilities expressed throughout the RLP and Lease. Please review the RLP and all attachments carefully paying particular attention to the solicitation requirements. The requirements for consideration of award will entail a complete bid that consists of the following criteria at a minimum: (Note: There may be other required forms. Refer to the enclosed RLP for details.): Initialed acceptance and use of government Lease indicating that you understand the Government�s terms and requirements. (Exhibit A Recruiting Form L100) 2. Initialed acceptance and use of government General Clauses Form 3517B indicating that you understand the Government�s terms and requirements. (Exhibit B Form 3517B General Clauses) 3. Competitive rates of base cost per square feet for annual rent and a breakout of operating expenses, Real Estate Taxes, and Janitorial service costs and Utilities. (Completed Exhibit C Proposal to Lease). 4. All costs and materials affiliated to meet the requirements of the construction specifications including all safety and security enhancements will be considered Tenant Improvements with no reimbursement from the government upon completion of the construction or through amortization within the Lease (Completed Exhibit F Construction Bid Worksheet). Do not attempt to complete the Lease form (USACE Recruiting Lease Form L100). Neither the RLP nor any other part of an Offeror�s proposal shall be part of the Lease except to the extent expressly incorporated therein. Please review all the documents thoroughly so that you have a complete understanding of the Government�s requirements. After receipt of all proposals, conclusions of any discussions, and receipt of best and final offers, the Government will select a location based on the lowest overall cost and technical requirements specified in the enclosed RLP. Past performance, if applicable, will also be taken into consideration. The selection is expected to occur approximately thirty (30) days following the initial proposal response date. A Government market survey, appraisal, or value estimate will be conducted to determine fair market rental value. title: Greece, Lithuania, Poland, Cyprus – Research and experimental development services – Pre-CommerciAl ProCuremenT of Innovative Personal ProtectiVe Equipment for First REsponders (ACTIVE PCP)
description: The Pre-CommerciAl ProCuremenT of Innovative Personal ProtectiVe Equipment for First REsponders (ACTIVE PCP) project addresses critical gaps in personal protective equipment (PPE). It responds to the need to keep first responders safe and operationally effective during evolving threats, from CBRN incidents and HAZMAT situations to terrorism, industrial accidents, natural disasters, and other complex emergencies. ACTIVE PCP involves public safety buyers and end-users in defining unmet needs and guiding industry R&D towards solutions. ACTIVE PCP procures R&D services through Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP). // Tenderers are invited to propose innovative PPE solutions for first responders, police, firefighters, and emergency medical services operating in complex CBRN and HAZMAT environments. Following the phased PCP model, the procurement supports R&D up to the development of a limited volume of first products. It comprises 3 competitive Phases, with fewer Tenderers progressing at each stage so that those offering the strongest response to the PCP's technical challenge are selected. // The PCP will be implemented by means of a Framework Agreement (FA) with call-offs for specific contracts for each of the 3 R&D phases (altogether ‘Contracts’). Greek law governs the Contracts. The GDPR Processing Agreement – if applicable – will be governed by the law of the Member State in which each pilot will take place during Phase 3. The FA will remain binding for the duration of all phases for which Contractors remain in the PCP. There will be no renegotiations. // KEMEA will be the Lead Procurer throughout all the phases of ACTIVE PCP. // Tenderers that are awarded a FA will also be awarded a specific contract for Phase 1 (evaluation of tenders for the FA and Phase 1 are combined). Tenderers are therefore asked not only to submit their detailed offer for Phase 1, but also to state their goals, and to outline their plans (including price conditions) for Phases 2 and 3. // The three Phases are: (i) Phase 1: Solution Design. A FA and a Specific Contract for Phase 1 will be awarded to at least six (6) contractors; (ii) Phase 2: Prototyping. A call-off will be organised for Phase 2, with the aim of awarding at least three (3) Phase 2 contracts. Only offers from Contractors that successfully completed Phase 1 will be eligible for Phase 2. The procurers will validate the Phase 2 prototypes; and (iii) Phase 3: Original development and testing. A second call-off will be organised for Phase 3, with the aim of awarding a minimum of two (2) Phase 3 contracts. Only offers from Contractors that successfully completed Phase 2 will be eligible for Phase 3. The procurers will validate the Phase 3 prototypes. // Offers for the next phase will be requested together with the End of Phase deliverables of the previous phase. I.e., all Contractors of the previous phase have the right to submit offers for the next phase (together with their End of Phase Report). A Contractor must have been awarded a Specific Contract for Phase 1 in order to be considered eligible for Phase 2. Likewise, a Contractor must have been awarded Specific Contracts for Phases 1 and 2 in order to be considered eligible for Phase 3. The maximum total budget for this PCP is 3.650.000 EUR including VAT, taxes and other related fees and costs). // The maximum budget per phase and the maximum budget per Contractor (excluding VAT, including taxes and other related fees and costs) are as follows: For Phase 1 (Solution Design): Subcontracting cost per contractor: €47,043.00; Total subcontracting cost for phase 1: €282,258.05. For Phase 2 (Prototyping): Subcontracting cost per contractor: €483,870.97; Total subcontracting cost for phase 2: €1,451,612.90. For Phase 3 (Original development and testing): Subcontracting cost per contractor: €604,838.71; Total subcontracting cost for phase 3: €1,209,677.42. For Phase 1, contracts will be financed until the remaining budget is insufficient to fund the next best tender. The exact number of contracts finally awarded will thus depend on the prices offered and the number of Tenders passing the evaluation. The lower the offered price of Tenders, the more contracts can be awarded. However, the total value of the contracts awarded can also be lower than initially expected if there are fewer tenders than expected that meet the minimum evaluation criteria. // Unless otherwise stated in the Call Off for Phase 2, contracts will be financed until the remaining budget is insufficient to fund the next best Tender. The exact number of contracts finally awarded will thus depend on the prices offered and the number of tenders passing the evaluation. The lower the offered price of Tenders, the more contracts can be awarded. However, the total value of the contracts awarded can also be lower than initially expected if there are fewer tenders than expected that meet the minimum evaluation criteria. // Unless otherwise stated in the Call Off for Phase 3, contracts for Phase 3 will be financed until the remaining budget is insufficient to fund the next best tender. The exact number of contracts finally awarded will thus depend on the prices offered and the number of tenders passing the evaluation. The lower the offered price of Tenders, the more contracts can be awarded. However, the total value of the contracts awarded can also be lower than initially expected if there are fewer tenders than expected that meet the minimum evaluation criteria. // As leftover budget from the previous phase can be transferred to the next phase(s), the total budget available for Phases 2 and/or 3 may eventually be higher than stated here (but the maximum budget per Contractor for Phases 2 and 3 will remain the same). // Further information on ACTIVE PCP as well as the Tender Documents can be found at https://www.activepcp.eu/

title: Kajaanin lentoaseman kutsupohjainen liityntäliikenne, henkilöliikenteen kuljetuspalvelu lentoasemalle ja asemalta maakuntaan Kajaanin AMK:n Kajaanin lentoaseman liityntäliikennepilotin kehittäminen ja markkinointi? -hankkeessa
description: Kajaanin ammattikorkeakoulun Kajaanin lentoaseman liityntäliikennepilotin kehittäminen ja markkinointi -hanke pyytää tarjousta Kajaanin lentoaseman liityntäliikenteen kutsupohjaisesta toteutuksesta kolmella (reitillä) ja niiden osatoteutuksista Kainuun alueella. Kutsupohjainen liityntäliikenteen pilotti, joka palvelee Kajaanin lentoaseman ja Kainuun kuntien välisiä yhteyksiä. Pilotoinnin kesto on n. 16 viikkoa ja toteutaan 10.12.2026 - 31.3.2027 välisenä aikana. Tilaaja varaa option jatkaa yhteistyötä mallin mukaisesti määrärahojen puitteissa pilotointiajan jälkeen ja sopeuttaa sitä sopimaan kulloinkin voimassa olevaan lentoliikenteen vuoroaikatauluun. Kuljetuspilotin reittejä on kolmeen (3) eri pääsuuntaan ja niiden osatoteutuksista Kainuun alueella ja liikenteestä Kajaanin kaupungin keskustaan. Kaikki reitit lähtevät tai loppuvat Kajaanin lentoasemalle. Reitit kulkevat kuntakeskuksissa linja-autoasemien tai muiden määriteltyjen keskeisten pysäkkien kautta huomioiden sesongin. Kuljetus vain niiltä osin kuin matkustajia on kyydissä. title: Core Environmental Compliance Support Services � Darby Military Community (DMC), USAG Italy
description: The 414th Contracting Support Brigade (RCO Italy) intends to issue a competitive Request for Quotation (RFQ) for professional, non-personal Core Environmental Compliance Support Services at the Darby Military Community (DMC) in Pisa/Livorno, Italy. The Contractor shall act as an independent environmental compliance consultant, providing specialized services to support the environmental engineering and compliance program for the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) Environmental Division (ED). The core tasks are structured under the following seven (7) functional areas: Environmental Plan Administration: Review, update, and maintain environmental media management plans (including Drinking Water, Storm Water, Solid Waste, Spill Response, and Asbestos) IAW the Italian Final Governing Standards (IFGS). Environmental Review Program Management: Coordinate the environmental review process for Garrison construction projects, including drafting Records of Environmental Consideration (RECs) and Requests for Environmental Review (RERs). Bilingual Training & Spill Exercises: Coordinate and conduct Hazardous Waste Handler (HWH) and Hazardous Material Handler (HMH) classroom training sessions and mock spill response exercises in both English and Italian. Compliance Inspections: Conduct monthly compliance assessments of Hazardous Waste Accumulation Points (HWAPs), motor pools, and aboveground/underground storage tanks, and annual inspections of air and wastewater assets. Database Management: Input and maintain environmental quality tracking data in standard military administrative systems (WEBCASS, SWAR Web, and Installation Status Reports). Host-Nation Permitting Support: Prepare technical engineering documentation to support permit requests and renewals with regional Italian authorities in accordance with Italian Legislative Decree D.Lgs. 152/06. Environmental Monitoring Support: Assist the Garrison in verifying that third-party sampling companies perform water and air monitoring in accordance with contract specifications. III. Special OCONUS / Host-Nation Eligibility Requirements (Mandatory) This procurement is restricted to firms legally established and registered to do business within the Host Nation of Italy. Offerors must meet the following mandatory criteria at the time of proposal submission: Chamber of Commerce (CCIAA) Registration: The offeror must possess a valid, active registration in the Italian Registry of Businesses (Registro delle Imprese) maintained by the local Chamber of Commerce, Industry, Handicraft, and Agriculture (CCIAA), and possess an active Italian VAT number (Partita IVA). Work Authorization: All proposed personnel must be Italian citizens or possess valid, pre-existing Italian work residency and authorization. The Contractor is solely responsible for complying with all Italian labor laws, national collective contracts (CCNL), social security requirements (INPS/INAIL), and employment reporting (including "Centro per l'impiego" documentation). No SOFA Status Sponsorship: The Government will not sponsor or grant Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA) status, tax-exempt privileges, or military-accredited work visas (under the DOCPER process) for any contractor personnel under this contract. IV. Mandatory System for Award Management (SAM) Registration In accordance with FAR 52.204-7, all prospective contractors must be registered and active in the System for Award Management (SAM) database prior to submitting an offer. Offerors must possess an active Unique Entity ID (UEI) and CAGE/NCAGE code registered in SAM. Offers received from companies not active and registered in SAM at the time of proposal submission will be determined legally ineligible for award. Registration can be completed at no cost at www.sam.gov. V. Key Personnel & Language Standards Contract Manager: Minimum of three (3) years of experience within the past five (5) years managing professional services or environmental consulting contracts. On-Site Expert: Master�s degree (diploma di laurea quinquennale) in an environmental-related field of study OR a Bachelor�s degree in an environmental field combined with a minimum of three (3) additional years of specialized professional environmental compliance experience in Italy. Language Proficiency: Proposed personnel must meet the Interagency Language Roundtable (ILR) Level 4 (Professional Performance Proficiency) or the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) Level C1/C2 (Proficient User) standard in both written and spoken English and Italian. Post-Award Onboarding: Prior experience with closed US military databases (WEBCASS, SWAR Web, ISR) is preferred but not mandatory. The proposed on-site expert must demonstrate the technical capability to become fully proficient in these military systems within thirty (30) calendar days of contract award and system access. VI. title: SPECIAL MISSIONS TRAINING CENTER LIVE-FIRE MARITIME/URBAN TRAINING SYSTEM
description: Purpose: The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) for market-research purposes to identify capable sources; available commercial solutions; current industry practices; potential acquisition approaches; and relevant technical, schedule, lifecycle-support, and cost information for the design, engineering, fabrication, delivery, installation, integration, testing, certification/validation, and commissioning of a Joint Maritime Training Facility (JMTF) live-fire maritime/urban training system. Site Visit Location: Participants are requested to assemble at The Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune Provost Marshal�s Office is located in Building 58 on Virginia Dare Drive, Camp Lejeune, North Carolina. Date: November 10, 2026 The contemplated requirement is for a complete and operational live-fire training system at the USCG Special Missions Training Center (SMTC), Courthouse Bay, Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, North Carolina. The facility must support realistic, modular, multi-level tactical training, including maritime interdiction, close-quarters combat, vertical access, breaching, and related joint-service mission sets. The system must integrate ballistic containment with maritime and urban training features and be suitable for repeated use in an outdoor coastal environment. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 236220. Disclaimer: There is no solicitation at this time. This RFI is not a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this request is purely voluntary; the Government will not pay for any costs incurred nor is obligated to respond. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. After reviewing RFI responses to this RFI, and if the USCG still plans to proceed with the acquisition, a solicitation announcement may be published on the Contract Opportunities (formerly FedBizOpps) website or distributed to contract holders if a strategically-sourced vehicle is deemed appropriate. It is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor the Contract Opportunities website. Failure to respond or submit sufficiently detailed information may result in a company not being considered a likely offeror when making a decision on whether or how to set aside a solicitation for restricted competition. Regardless of the information submitted, the Government reserves the right to consider any arrangement as determined appropriate for this requirement. No proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response to this RFI. The Government reserves the right to use any information provided by respondents for any purpose determined necessary and legally appropriate, including using technical information provided by respondents in any resultant solicitation. The anticipated contractor would provide all labor, supervision, project management, engineering, materials, equipment, transportation, installation, testing, documentation, commissioning, and training necessary to deliver a complete live-fire maritime/urban training facility. The anticipated effort includes: Complete facility design and engineering, including ballistic, structural, civil, architectural, mechanical, electrical, fire/life-safety, safety, and training-system interfaces. Preparation of a Design Basis Report; design packages; calculations; submittals; shop and fabrication drawings; installation plans; final as-built drawings; and operations and maintenance (O&M) manuals. Fabrication, delivery, installation, integration, testing, ballistic certification or validation, commissioning, and Government acceptance support. A ballistic wall and containment system rated and validated for the Government-approved firing geometry, engagement distances, and training conditions, with a planning threat basis of 6.8 mm XM1188E1 ammunition, with an additional 12-inch layer of sacrificial ballistic rubber blocks or an appropriate bullet-trap target system. Projectile-management and ricochet-mitigation surfacing; reconfigurable ballistic panels; and portable bullet traps. A multi-level training system incorporating urban, maritime, and lower-deck training areas; configurable rooms and corridors; ship-type doors and hatches; ladders; grated decks; confined passageways; vertical-access/rappelling features; observation catwalks; and instructor viewing platforms. Foundations, slabs, structural framing, site preparation, drainage, lighting, electrical distribution, ventilation/air exchange, weather protection, fire detection/alarm components, emergency egress, and other systems required for the approved design. Corrosion resistance and weather protection appropriate for a coastal Camp Lejeune environment. Operator/instructor training, maintenance training, recommended spare-parts lists, inspection checklists, maintenance schedules, and lifecycle-support recommendations. Project management, recurring coordination meetings, progress reporting, integrated scheduling, and coordination with Camp Lejeune access, safety, security, delivery, and range-operation requirements. The anticipated period of performance will not exceed 300 calendar days from date of award or Notice to Proceed. The primary place of performance will be Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, North Carolina; design and fabrication may occur at contractor facilities. The Government�s planning material includes differing conceptual dimensions�an approximately 50-foot by 120-foot live-fire footprint and an approximately 140-foot by 70-foot overall concept footprint with a tower-deck elevation of approximately 30 feet. Respondents should identify their recommended dimensions, elevations, clearances, and facility configuration, along with the assumptions supporting their recommendation. Include the contract number, administering agency, contract scope, ordering limitations, and agency point-of-contact information. Relevant capability and past-performance summary. Describe organizational experience with comparable live-fire facilities, ballistic containment systems, tactical training systems, maritime or urban training features, multi-level towers, range safety systems, and coastal-environment construction. title: Cost Effective On-Base Parcel Delivery Solutions (RAFL, RAFM, RAFF, United Kingdom)
description: The 48th Contracting Squadron at Royal Air Force (RAF) Lakenheath, United Kingdom, seeks to identify qualified sources and cost-effective commercially practical solutions capable of providing reliable on-base parcel delivery services for RAF Lakenheath (RAFL), RAF Mildenhall (RAFM), and RAF Feltwell (RAFF) in the United Kingdom. Purpose of Market Research: Our primary objective is to gain an understanding of how the Government's required delivery outcome can be achieved at a reasonable/sustainable cost while also being reliable. The Government is not seeking an unnecessarily complex or premium delivery model where a simpler commercial solution could reliably satisfy the requirement. *This RFI is issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or promise to issue a future solicitation. Responses are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparation or submission of information in response to this RFI. * Background: Personnel who live or work on RAFL, RAFM, and RAF Feltwell receive both personal and official parcels from commercial delivery companies. The most common carriers, presently, have been DPD, DHL, Evri, FedEx, Parcelforce, UPS, Amazon, and Royal Mail. Royal Mail/Parcelforce are the only delivery entities that presently have installation access and deliver directly to the on-base addresses. Other commercial parcel delivery companies do not have installation access, creating challenges in completing delivery to the intended on-base residence or agency. The Government is exploring a recurring parcel delivery service capable of receiving or otherwise obtaining parcels from commercial carriers that do not have installation access and completing final delivery to the intended residence or agency on RAF Lakenheath, RAF Mildenhall, or RAF Feltwell. The Government seeks industry�s recommendations regarding the most efficient and economical means of accomplishing this outcome. Packages, after they are picked up by a neighbor, have an average dwell time of 2 weeks before the intended recipients of the packages become aware that a neighbor had received their package on their behalf. The Government is particularly interested in solutions that make use of existing commercial capabilities and minimize unnecessary Government-specific processes, facilities, equipment, or infrastructure. Primary Constraints: Installation access and funding will be the primary constraints and will be the biggest factors considered in developing the desired solution. Presently installation access for local nationals can take upwards of 7 months due to the MOD clearance/background check process. The government is not aware of any route to expedite the processing of packages. It has been observed that the delivery driver experiences a high level of turnover, unpredictable routes for drivers, and criminal records that prohibit access to the installation which affects the parcel delivery companies� ability to obtain installation access for their drivers. Drones are not permitted on or near these installations and should not be included in identified solutions. Government-provided escorts will not be available as an interim staffing or access solution. Respondents should consider these conditions when describing their proposed solution and should identify how they could achieve the required staffing and access capability within the anticipated transition period. Respondents should also identify cost-effective approaches for maintaining sufficient access-qualified staffing without unnecessarily increasing the number of personnel requiring installation access. Estimated Parcel Volume: Available information indicates that approximately 1,000 parcels per week are associated with RAF Lakenheath that are being coordinated for pick-up at businesses near the installation. Should a reliable delivery service be established, the volume of parcels is expected to at least triple. Comparable parcel-volume information is not currently available for RAFM or RAFF. The bases in order of highest estimated volume to lowest are as follows: RAFL, RAFF, RAFM. All quantities provided in this RFI are estimates for market research and planning purposes and should not be interpreted as guaranteed quantities or maximum quantities. Suggested solutions will need to be scalable to fluctuate as personnel to the bases fluctuate and parcel volume fluctuates. Respondents should identify how uncertainty and fluctuations in parcel volume would affect their recommended solution and pricing. Respondents are also encouraged to suggest a Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) structure best suited to their recommendation. Respondents are specifically encouraged to identify approaches that allow the service to scale efficiently as parcel volume changes without requiring the Government to pay for unnecessary excess capacity during lower-volume periods. Desired Outcome: The desired outcome is a reliable and cost-effective service capable of delivering eligible parcels from commercial delivery companies that do not have installation access to the residence or agency on the installation that ordered the item. The service would be expected to support RAFL, RAFM, and RAFF. All three installations are anticipated to be included from the very beginning of performance. The service would handle both personal and official parcels. Delivery service is expected seven days per week. For residential deliveries, parcels that do not require a recipient signature may be left at the recipient's door (or in a safe place designated by their delivery notes). The Government recognizes that commercial carriers may transfer parcels at different times throughout the day. Respondents should identify any operational assumptions, carrier coordination, cutoff times, or other conditions necessary to accomplish daily delivery. Solutions should not be disruptive, so the preference is to find a solution to deliver packages by 1700 each day ensuring no nighttime disruptions. If a requirement or assumption described in this RFI would have a significant impact on the cost, please identify the cost driver and recommend a less expensive alternative that would still provide reliable on-base parcel delivery. Commercial Carrier Coordination The Government has not established the required method for obtaining parcels from commercial carriers that lack installation access. Respondents should recommend solutions. If multiple solutions are available, you are encouraged to make multiple recommendations. The Government is interested in understanding how industry could establish effective and economical means of accepting, collecting, transferring, consolidating, or otherwise obtaining custody of eligible parcels from commercial delivery companies and subsequently completing final delivery to the appropriate on-base residence or agency. The Government has not determined whether an on-base facility, off-base facility, consolidation point, direct carrier transfer, existing commercial facility, existing delivery network, or another method represents the most effective solution. Respondents should identify the approach they recommend and any Government support, facilities, infrastructure, or coordination that would be necessary for that approach. *There is a preference for practical solutions leveraging existing commercial operations, avoiding the creation of dedicated infrastructure where it is not necessary to achieve the required outcome. * Package Manifest/Security Information Packages entering the installations must be supported by appropriate manifest information or a form of documentation of items being transported/number of packages being delivered. Ideally, security forces would have visibility of the items contained within individual packages when
